title: Protected reference outline: Production-Ready Linux Server Platform
answer: Reference approach: define the scope and threat/safety boundaries; build a small working path using synthetic data or disposable VMs; implement the required features in steps; add repeatable tests and a dry-run/verification phase; collect expected and actual output; document failures, limitations, backup/rollback steps, and how another person can reproduce the result. For any production-oriented feature, verify it in an isolated test environment before deployment. Required project outcomes: Repeatable server setup and documented baseline; Non-root application execution and controlled admin access; Verified SSH, firewall policy, and HTTPS; Managed service and structured logs; Metrics, health checks, and actionable alerts; Automated backups with demonstrated restore; Version-controlled operations scripts and configuration management; Troubleshooting runbooks, security review, and performance measurements; Deployment verification and rollback plan.
explanation: The project should be assessed from the submitted artifacts and observed evidence. A starter scaffold or a running service alone is not proof that security, monitoring, backups, restore, compatibility, or rollback requirements are met.
evidence_checklist: Source files are organized and documented.
Automated or manual tests cover normal and boundary/failure cases.
Observed output and versions are recorded.
Security and least-privilege decisions are explained.
Backup/restore or rollback has been demonstrated where relevant.
Known limitations and any untested steps are stated clearly.
